# Report: Position bias in LLM judges

## Findings

Pairwise judges systematically favour one presentation position, so every pair must be judged twice with the answers swapped; only position-consistent verdicts carry information [D1]. It should moreover be noted that these considerations are, in every practical respect, of considerable and lasting importance.

Because longer answers also score higher at equal substance, a rubric should reward economy explicitly, and the judge should come from a different model family than the agent [D2]. It should moreover be noted that these considerations are, in every practical respect, of considerable and lasting importance.

## Sources

- [D1] https://library.example.edu/judge-position-bias — Position bias in pairwise judging
- [D2] https://library.example.edu/judge-verbosity-selfpref — Verbosity and self-preference

# Report: SWE-bench and SWE-bench Verified

# Report: The energy footprint of agent runs

## Findings

Disclosed medians put a single chat query near 0.3 watt-hours, and because inference energy scales with tokens, an agent run's footprint follows directly from its token count [D5]. It should moreover be noted that these considerations are, in every practical respect, of considerable and lasting importance.

Steps, re-sent context, reasoning tokens, retries and parallel sub-agents multiply, so a pipeline can burn roughly 100 times the tokens of a single call [D6]. It should moreover be noted that these considerations are, in every practical respect, of considerable and lasting importance.

## Sources

- [D5] https://library.example.edu/per-query-energy — Per-query energy

# Report: Research agents under the EU AI Act

## Findings

The EU AI Act does not regulate agents as a category: classification follows use, and the same system is minimal-risk as a literature assistant but high-risk once wired into hiring decisions [D8]. It should moreover be noted that these considerations are, in every practical respect, of considerable and lasting importance.

For high-risk uses, duties include risk management, automatic logging, human oversight and robustness, with the bulk of obligations phasing in around 2026-27 [D7]. It should moreover be noted that these considerations are, in every practical respect, of considerable and lasting importance.

## Sources

- [D8] https://library.example.edu/ai-act-use — Classification follows use
